Thanks Jamal  great questions. Short answers + recommended approach below. I’ve attached a one-pager that summarizes these levers.

1) Streaming + continuous batching:
- Continuous batching reduces per-token cost by aggregating requests but introduces an additional batching delay window. In practice we can keep first-token latency < 50 ms with a small batching window (5-10 ms) for high-QPS traffic. For low-QPS, we recommend hybrid routing: route latency-sensitive requests to a low-batch/low-latency pool and throughput-bound requests to a high-batch pool.
- For streaming specifically, we support token-by-token streaming from our runtime; batching affects the emit cadence but not the correctness of partial outputs.

2) Quantization profiles:
- We support int8 and int4 (Q4) profiles on supported model variants. Trade-offs: Q4 typically gives ~2-2.5x memory reduction and cost savings but may introduce minor regeneration/quality differences on tricky instructions or code-heavy prompts. We recommend a two-arm test: Q8 for canary + Q4 for cost-optimized traffic, with automated quality-monitoring (we can run evals on your sample prompts).

3) Caching (prefix / KV):
- For applications that reuse large common prefixes, we’ve seen token savings of 30-60% depending on prompt reuse. Your anonymized traces will help us estimate hit-rate. We can enable prefix caching at the route level and measure savings during the pilot.

4) Other levers:
- Model variants: run the same prompt across a smaller architecture variant for inexpensive fallback (good for best-effort responses).
- Dynamic routing: send long-context sessions to dedicated pools with larger KV cache.

Next steps I propose this week:
- You: send anonymized sample traces + qps histogram (thanks for committing to that).
- Us: Rishi will spin up a short bench (2-3 days) on a representative quantization/profile matrix (float32, int8, q4), with both streaming and non-streaming configs and continuous-batching windows. We’ll report: p50/p95/p99 first-token, per-token cost estimate, and cache hit simulation.
- Pilot timing: Nov 2 start is doable if we finalize scope this week.
